title: Thai Automotive Assembly Line Digital Twin
thesis: Snowflake turns daily readings from a synthetic digital twin of body weld cells, paint booths, trim and chassis stations and end-of-line test cells in six Thai plant cities into availability KPIs, 7-day line-stop risk scores, vibration anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Station availability, unplanned line stops, MTBF and stations twinned for 24 assembly stations across Rayong, Chonburi, Chachoengsao, Ayutthaya, Samut Prakan and Prachinburi.
Each KPI is an explicit numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, traceable to station-day rows.
The line-stop chart ranks stop causes by hours lost, from robot servo faults and weld tip wear to AGV guidance faults.
tabs.call_out: One governed twin of every assembly line in the network

transition.line: Which stations are likely to stop the line next?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each station's probability of stopping the line in the next 7 days.
The holdout line reports precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, next to the base rate, so the model is judged honestly.
Anomaly detection flags vibration outliers per station, and the forecast projects plant-network line-stop hours for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Evaluated ML that runs where the twin data lives

transition.line: Are the lineside spares and PM discipline there to respond?

talking_points: Parts on order and lineside spare coverage show whether weld tip kits, atomizer bell cups, torque tool transducers and dyno roller bearings are on hand.
PM compliance against first-pass yield by station shows where the two move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, line-stop and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human deciding

transition.line: What happens when a station alarms on the line right now?

talking_points: Live station readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the in-account simulator or from AWS IoT Core through S3 and Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the station's current risk band, then emails the on-call line engineer.
tabs.call_out: From station alarm to work instruction in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 15 synthetic line-stop SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOP IDs it cited.
tabs.call_out: Natural-language answers that can be audited

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic, seeded demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
